en: A person who learns from another, especially one who then teaches others.
An active follower or adherent of someone, or some philosophy etc.
To convert (a person) into a disciple.
To train, educate, teach.

disciple.ety: From Middle English disciple, discipul, from Old English discipul (“disciple, scholar”), from Latin discipulus (“pupil, learner”). Later influenced or superseded in Middle English by Old French deciple.

ex.en: When the two disciples heard him say this, they followed Jesus.
ex.ja: 二人の弟子は、彼がそう言うのを聞いて、イエスについていった。

ex.en: However the disciples awoke to that danger.
ex.ja: しかし、使徒たちはその危険に気付いた。

ex.en: The next day John was there again with two of his disciples.
ex.ja: その翌日。またヨハネは、二人の弟子と共に立っていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 discipulus（生徒）から。discere（学ぶ）。「弟子」。discipline（教え・規律）と同じ。

en: The act or state of deliberately not paying attention or caring about something.
To ignore; to pay no attention to.

ex.en: He has a disregard for the law.
ex.ja: 彼は法律を構わず無視する。

ex.en: Sorry. I said too much. Disregard what I just said.
ex.ja: ごめん。言い過ぎた。今、私が言ったことは、気にしないで。

ex.en: Didn't you disregard a stop sign?
ex.ja: 停止標識を無視しませんでしたか。

note.ja: dis（否定）+ regard（注意を払う）。「無視する」。

A device that distributes electric current, especially to the spark plugs in an internal combustion engine.

en: Power or the use of power; sovereignty over something; stewardship, supremacy.
Predominance; ascendancy.

dominion.ety: From Middle English dominion, from Middle French dominion, from Latin dominium (“lordship, right of ownership”), from dominus (“lord”), from domus (“house”). See demain, demesne, domain, dominium.

ex.en: Does mankind have dominion over animals and birds?
ex.ja: 人間は鳥や動物を支配しているだろうか。

note.ja: ラテン語 dominium（所有・支配）から。dom（主人）。→「支配権・領土・自治領」。

en: Down a slope.
So as to deteriorate or get worse.
Located towards or at the bottom of a slope or hill.
Going down a slope or a hill.
The fastest of the disciplines of alpine skiing.
A rapid descent of a hill in related sports, especially in alpine skiing.
To take part in downhill skiing.

ex.en: For a girl, after 30, it's downhill all the way.
ex.ja: 女は３０を過ぎてからはずっと下り坂だ。

ex.en: The weather is supposed to go downhill starting this afternoon.
ex.ja: 午後から天気は下り坂になります。

note.ja: down（下へ）+ hill（丘）。「坂を下って」→「悪化して」。

en: Genuinely horrific, awful, or alarming; dangerous, risky.
Unpleasant, awful, very bad (also used as an intensifier).
Dreadfully.
A shocker: a report of a crime written in a provokingly lurid style.
A journal or broadsheet printing such reports.

dreadful.ety: From Middle English dredful, dredfull, dredeful (also dreful). By surface analysis, dread + -ful.

ex.en: I had a feeling that something dreadful was happening.
ex.ja: 何か恐ろしいことが起こりそうな気がした。

ex.en: A dreadful accident happened on the corner.
ex.ja: 町角で恐ろしい事故が起きた。

ex.en: I had a dreadful dream last night.
ex.ja: 昨夜恐ろしい夢を見ました。

note.ja: dread（恐れ）+ -ful。「恐ろしい」→「ひどい」。

en: To remove (markings or information).
To obliterate information from (a storage medium), such as to clear or (with magnetic storage) to demagnetize.
The operation of deleting data.

ex.en: Their names were erased from the list.
ex.ja: 彼らの名前はリストから削られた。

ex.en: He erased his speech from the tape.
ex.ja: 彼はテープから自分の演説を消した。

ex.en: I tried to erase the memory of her crying.
ex.ja: 私は彼女が涙を流した思い出を忘れようと努めた。

note.ja: ラテン語 eradere（こすり取る）から。e（外へ）+ radere（こする）。「消す」。razor と同じ。

en: Having had population removed, by evacuation.
Containing a vacuum.

ex.en: The people were evacuated because of the flood.
ex.ja: 大水のため人々は立ち退いた。

en: Of feelings, a person's spirit, a state of affairs, etc.: put out, as if like a fire; quenched, suppressed.
Of customs, ideas, laws and legal rights, offices, organizations, languages, etc.: no longer existing or in use; defunct, discontinued, o…

extinct.ety: From Late Middle English extinct (“eliminated, eradicated, extinguished”), from Latin extīnctus, exstīnctus (“extinguished, quenched; destroyed, killed; made extinct”), the perfect passive participles of extinguō, exstinguō (“to extinguish, put out, quench; (figurative) to abolish; to destroy, kill”), from ex- (prefix meaning ‘away; out’) + stinguō (“to extinguish, put out, quench”) (from Proto-Indo-European *stengʷ- (“to push”)). The Middle English word displaced Middle English aqueint, aquenched (“extinct; extinguished”). Doublet of extinguish.

ex.en: This custom became extinct a long time ago.
ex.ja: この習慣は絶えて久しい。

ex.en: Dinosaurs became extinct a very long time ago.
ex.ja: 恐竜は大昔に絶滅した。

ex.en: Unless whales are protected, they will become extinct.
ex.ja: 鯨は保護されなければ、絶滅するだろう。

note.ja: ラテン語 exstinctus（消された）から。「（火が）消えた」→「絶滅した」。extinction と同じ。

en: To disallow; to proscribe.
To deny, exclude from, or warn off, by express command.

forbid.ety:
From Middle English forbeden, from Old English forbēodan (“to forbid, prohibit, restrain, refuse, repeal, annul”), from Proto-Germanic *furibeudaną, from *furi + *beudaną. Equivalent to for- (“from, away”) + bid (“to offer, proclaim”). Cognate with Dutch verbieden (“to forbid”), German verbieten (“to forbid”), Danish forbyde (“to forbid”),
Norwegian Bokmål forby (“to forbid”), Swedish förbjuda (“to forbid”), Gothic 𐍆𐌰𐌿𐍂𐌱𐌹𐌿𐌳𐌰𐌽 (faurbiudan). Related to forbode.

ex.en: My parents forbade me to see Tom again.
ex.ja: 両親は私がまたトムと会うことを禁止した。

ex.en: My father forbids me to go out at night.
ex.ja: 父は私が夜外出するのを禁止している。

ex.en: I forbid smoking in my room.
ex.ja: 私の部屋での喫煙を禁ずる。

note.ja: for（反対に）+ bid（命じる）。「しないように命じる」→「禁じる」。forbidden。

en: An appliance or room used to store food or other perishable items at temperatures below 0° Celsius (32° Fahrenheit).
The section of a refrigerator used to store food or other perishable items at a temperature below 0° Celsius (32° Fahrenheit).

ex.ja: 私が冷凍庫を持つ十分な理由がいくつかある。

note.ja: freeze（凍らせる）+ -er。「冷凍庫」。

en: In a manner relating to genes or genetics.
In terms of origin or development.

ex.en: Do you think it's dangerous to eat genetically modified food?
ex.ja: 遺伝子組み換え食品を食べるのは危険だと思いますか？

ex.en: Many consumers are concerned about the health risks of genetically modified food.
ex.ja: 多くの消費者が遺伝子組み換え食品の健康リスクについて懸念を示している。

ex.en: You probably eat genetically modified fruits and vegetables all the time without knowing it.
ex.ja: おそらく知らず知らずのうちに遺伝子組み換えの果物や野菜をいつも口にしているだろう。

en: Any of several plant-eating mammals of the genus Lepus, similar to a rabbit, but larger and with longer ears.
The meat from this animal.
To move swiftly.
Grey, hoary; grey-haired, venerable (of people).
Cold, frosty (of weather).

hare.ety:
From Middle English hare, from Old English hara (“hare”), from Proto-West Germanic *hasō ~ *haʀ-, from Proto-Germanic *hesô, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱh₂s-én-; possibly related to or influenced by Proto-Germanic *haswaz (“grey”).
Cognates
See also West Frisian hazze, Dutch haas, German Hase, Norwegian and Swedish hare, Icelandic heri), Old English hasu, Middle High German heswe (“pale, dull”); also Welsh cannu (“to whiten”), ceinach (“hare”), Latin cānus (“white”), cascus (“old”), Old Prussian sasnis (“hare”), Pashto سوی (soe, “hare”) and Sanskrit शश (śaśa, “hare”).

ex.en: He is as mad as a March hare.
ex.ja: 彼は、３月の野ウサギのように狂っているよ。

ex.en: He who runs after two hares will catch neither.
ex.ja: 二兎を追う者は一兎をも得ず。

ex.en: First, catch your hare, then cook him.
ex.ja: まず現物を手に入れよ。

note.ja: 古英語 hara から。「野ウサギ」。rabbit より大きく耳が長い。

en: In this; within this content, context, or thing.

herein.ety: From Middle English here-inne, her-in, her-inne, hier-ine, from Old English hērinne, from Proto-West Germanic *hērinna, from Proto-Germanic *hē₂rinna, equivalent to here + in. Cognate with West Frisian hjiryn (“herein”), Dutch hierin (“herein”), German hierin (“herein”), Danish heri (“herein”), Swedish häri (“herein”), Icelandic hér í (“herein”).

en: Given as an honor, with no duties attached, and without payment.
Voluntary.
A person who holds an honorary appointment.
A kind of secret society that operates in name only, with membership given to honor some achievement.

honorary.ety: From honor + -ary, modelled after French honoraire, from Latin honōrārius.

ex.en: The college bestowed an honorary degree on him.
ex.ja: 大学は彼に名誉学位を与えた。

ex.en: General Franks received an honorary knighthood.
ex.ja: フランクス陸軍大将がナイト爵位の名誉称号を授かりました。

note.ja: ラテン語 honorarius（名誉の）から。honor。「名誉の」。honorarium（謝礼金）も同じ。

en: Not fully formed or developed; not grown.
Childish in behavior; juvenile.
An immature member of a species.

immature.ety: From Middle French immature. Partially displaced unripe, from Old English unrīpe (“unripe, immature”).

note.ja: im（否定）+ mature（成熟した）。「未熟な」。

To create a stitch by pulling the working yarn through an existing stitch from back to front.
A knitted garment.
A session of knitting.

en: Having the characteristics of a man.
Having qualities viewed as befitting a man; masculine, manful, courageous, resolute, noble.
In a way befitting a man.

manly.ety:
From Middle English manli, manlich, manly, from Old English *manlīċ (suggested by adverb manlīċe (“in a way befitting a person; nobly, stately”)), from Proto-West Germanic *mannlīk, from Proto-Germanic *mannlīkaz, equivalent to man + -ly (adjectival suffix).
Cognate with Old High German manlīh (“manly”) (whence German männlich), Dutch mannelijk, Old Norse mannligr (“human”) (Danish mandlig, Swedish manlig).

ex.en: He is a silent, manly boy.
ex.ja: 彼は無口で男らしい少年だ。

ex.en: Tom isn't very manly.
ex.ja: トムはあまり男らしくない。

ex.en: It is not manly to speak ill of others behind their backs.
ex.ja: 他人の悪口をかげで言うのは男らしくない。

note.ja: man + -ly。「男らしい」。

en: The state of being a mother; motherhood.
The state of being pregnant; pregnancy.

maternity.ety: From French maternité, from Latin māternitās.

ex.en: She will start her maternity leave next week.
ex.ja: 彼女は来週から産休に入る。

ex.en: I'll be on maternity leave from 30 September to 14 October.
ex.ja: ９月３０日から１０月１４日まで産休を取ります。

ex.en: After her maternity leave, she resumed her old job.
ex.ja: 産休のあと彼女はまたもとの仕事に戻った。

note.ja: mater（母）+ nity。母であること →「母性・出産・妊婦の」。maternity leave は「産休」。

en: Behavior that is considered to be unacceptable.
A penalty or write-up for improper behavior.
To mismanage.
To behave inappropriately, to misbehave.

ex.en: Jim got dismissed for his misconduct in office.
ex.ja: ジムは職権乱用で免職になった。

ex.en: She made an allusion to his misconduct.
ex.ja: 彼女は彼の不品行にそれとなくふれた。

ex.en: He was dismissed by the company for a misconduct.
ex.ja: 不正行為のため彼は解雇された。

note.ja: mis（悪く）+ conduct（行い）。「不正行為」。

en: Not having the power of speech; dumb.
Silent; not making a sound.
A person who does not have the power of speech.
A hired mourner at a funeral; an undertaker's assistant.
To silence, to make quiet.
To turn off the sound of.

ex.ja: 携帯はいつもミュートにしてます。

ex.en: Deaf-mute people talk using sign language.
ex.ja: 聾唖者は手話で話す。

en: Not needed; unnecessary.

needless.ety: From Middle English needlees, nedelees, nedeles, equivalent to need + -less.

ex.en: What did they add this needless function for?
ex.ja: こんな余計な機能なんでつけたんだろう。

ex.en: Needless to say, getting up early is important.
ex.ja: 言うまでもなく、早起きは大切です。

ex.en: Needless to say, he never came again.
ex.ja: 言うまでもないが、彼は二度と来なかった。

note.ja: need（必要）+ -less。「不必要な」。

en: The state of being new or novel; newness.
A new product; an innovation.
In the design of a common household item, often impractically large, and meant primarily for display rather than functional use.

novelty.ety: From Middle English novelte, from Old French novelté (Modern French nouveauté), from the adjective novel, ultimately from Latin novellus. By surface analysis, novel + -ty.

ex.en: A novelty wears off in time.
ex.ja: 新しいものはやがてすたれる。

note.ja: ラテン語 novellus（新しい）から。novus。「目新しさ」。novel、innovation と同じ nov。

en: A tendency to expect the best, or at least, a favourable outcome.
The doctrine that this world is the best of all possible worlds.

optimism.ety: From French optimisme, equivalent to Latin optimus + -ism.

ex.en: My father chose not to disturb my optimism.
ex.ja: 父は私の楽観を乱さないことにした。

ex.en: There is considerable optimism that the economy will improve.
ex.ja: 経済が好転するだろうという楽観論がかなりある。

note.ja: ラテン語 optimum（最良のもの）+ -ism。「楽観主義」。optimistic と同じ。

ex.ja: あなたの考えは、ちょっと古いんだって。

en: A member of the lowly social class that toils on the land, constituted by small farmers and tenants, sharecroppers, farmhands and other l…
A country person.
Characteristic of or relating to a peasant or peasants; unsophisticated.

peasant.ety:
From Late Middle English paissaunt, from Anglo-Norman paisant, from Old French païsant, païsan (“countryman, peasant”), from païs (“country”), from Latin pāgus (“countryside”) + Old French -enc (“member of”), from Frankish -inc, -ing "-ing"; which was an alteration of earlier Late Latin pāgēnsis (“inhabitant of a district”). Doublet of paisano.
Via Latin pāgus cognate with pagan (compare typologically, see there for more).

ex.en: Those peasants badly need land to grow rice.
ex.ja: それらの小作農は、米を作る土地をとても必要としている。

ex.en: I am nothing but a poor peasant.
ex.ja: 私は貧しい農民に過ぎない。

ex.en: I'm nothing but a poor peasant.
ex.ja: 私は貧しい農民に過ぎない。

note.ja: 古フランス語 paisant（田舎の人）から。pays（国・田舎）。「小作農・農民」。pagan（田舎の人 → 異教徒）と同系。

Beside the point.
A peripheral device.
Peripheral vision.

en: 20 fluid ounces, approximately 568 millilitres (an imperial pint).
16 US fluid ounces [473 millilitres] for liquids (a US liquid pint) or

pint.ety: From Middle English pinte, from Old French pinte, assumed from Vulgar Latin *pincta (“a mark used to indicate a level of quantity against a larger measure”), from Latin picta (“painted”), from Latin pingō (“paint”, verb). Doublet of pinto and Pinto.

ex.en: Two pints are equal to a quart.
ex.ja: ２パイントは１クオートと等しい。

ex.en: This beer mug holds one pint.
ex.ja: このジョッキは１パイント入る。

note.ja: 古フランス語 pinte から。液量の単位。イギリスのパブではビール1杯の量。

en: To present (an argument or a plea), especially in a legal case.
To beg, beseech, or implore, especially emotionally.

plead.ety: From Middle English pleden, plaiden, from Old French plaider (“to plead, offer a plea”), from plait, from Medieval Latin placitum (“a decree, sentence, suit, plea, etc.", in Classical Latin, "an opinion, determination, prescription, order; literally, that which is pleasing, pleasure”), neuter of placitus, past participle of placeō (“to please”). Cognate with Spanish pleitear (“to litigate, take to court”).

ex.en: Tom pleaded to his mother for money.
ex.ja: トムはお母さんにお金をねだった。

ex.en: The criminal pleaded with him to change his mind.
ex.ja: 罪人は考えを変えるよう彼に懇願した。

ex.en: Tom pleaded with his mother for money.
ex.ja: トムはお母さんにお金をねだった。

note.ja: 古フランス語 plaidier（訴える）から。plea と同じ。「嘆願する・申し立てる」。

en: To defecate.
To defecate in or on something.
Fecal matter; feces.
An act of defecation.
Expressing annoyed disappointment.

poop.ety: Uncertain, possibly from Middle English poupen (“to make a gulping sound while drinking, blow on a horn, toot”). Compare Dutch poepen (“to defecate”), German Low German pupen (“to fart; break wind”). Also representing poo pronounced with the mouth snapped closed at the end.

ex.en: I do not want to clean up dog poop.
ex.ja: 俺は犬のフンなんてかたづけたくない。

ex.en: Mom, I have to poop.
ex.ja: ママ、うんちしたい。

ex.en: My car is covered with pigeon poop.
ex.ja: 俺の車、鳩のフンまみれだよ。

en: The explicit literary or visual depiction of sexual subject matter; any display of material of an erotic nature.
The depiction of (non-sexual) subject matter so that it elicits feelings analogous to erotic pleasure; any such depiction.
To turn into pornography.

pornography.ety: Borrowed from French pornographie. By surface analysis, porno- + -graphy.

note.ja: ギリシャ語 pornē（娼婦）+ graphein（書く）。graph と同じ。

note.ja: prevalent（広まっている）+ -ence。pre（前に・上に）+ valere（強い）。「優勢であること」→「普及・蔓延」。

ex.ja: 今まで発音を間違えてたよ。

en: Temporary, but with the intention of eventually becoming permanent or being replaced by a permanent equivalent.
A postage stamp issued locally before an official issue is released.
An interim denture.

provisional.ety: From provision + -al, or else from Middle French provisionnal (modern French provisionnel). Compare Latin prōvīsiōnālis.

ex.en: We'll have our firm's attorneys look through the provisional agreement.
ex.ja: 社の弁護士に暫定合意の内容を吟味してもらおう。

note.ja: provision（備え）+ -al。pro（前もって）+ videre（見る）。「前もって備えた」→「暫定的な」。provide と同じ vid。

en: Synonym of pay back in all senses.
To make worthwhile; to yield a result worth the effort; to pay off.

repay.ety: From Old French repaier (“to pay back”), from re- + paiier (“to pay”), from Latin pācāre (“to settle, to make peaceful”), from pāx (“peace”) + -ō (forming verbs). Equivalent to re- + pay. Cognate with repacify and French repayer (“to pay again”).

ex.en: I think that he repaid the money.
ex.ja: 彼はお金を返したと思う。

ex.en: He promised to repay the money, but I doubt his word.
ex.ja: 彼はお金を返してくれると約束したが疑わしいと思う。

ex.en: I must repay the debt.
ex.ja: 借金を返さなければならない。

note.ja: re（元へ）+ pay（払う）。「返済する・報いる」。

en: Of a reddish pink colour.
Red or pink makeup to add colour to the cheeks; blusher.
Any reddish pink colour.
To apply rouge (makeup).

rouge.ety: Borrowed from French rouge, from Latin rubeus. Compare rare Middle English rouge, rouȝ (“red”); later borrowed again, as it is not attested until c. 1750. The game senses are of unknown origin according to the Oxford English Dictionary.

ex.en: Expressions and smiles change like that just from applying rouge and lipstick.
ex.ja: ほお紅や口紅を差すだけで表情や笑顔がどんどん変わってくるんです。

note.ja: フランス語 rouge（赤）から。ラテン語 rubeus。ruby と同じ。「頬紅」。

en: UK, Canada, New Zealand, Australia, and Ireland spelling of rumor.
Commonwealth standard spelling of rumor.

rumour.ety: From Middle English rumour, from Old French rumour, rumor, from Latin rūmor (“common talk”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *rewH- (“to shout, roar”).

ex.en: That rumour is not true, is it?
ex.ja: そのうわさは本当ではないでしょうね。

ex.en: Who did you hear that rumour from?
ex.ja: その噂、誰から聞いたの？

ex.en: From whom did you hear that rumour?
ex.ja: その噂、誰から聞いたの？

note.ja: rumor のイギリスのつづり。

en: Full; unable to hold or contain any more.
Soaked or drenched with moisture.
A saturated hydrocarbon.

ex.en: He saturated himself with sunshine.
ex.ja: 彼は日光を全身に浴びた。

note.ja: saturate（飽和させる）+ -ed。ラテン語 satur（満腹の）。「いっぱいに満たされた」→「飽和した」。satisfy と同じ sat。

en: Drenched with water, or other liquid.

ex.en: Tom was completely soaked by the rain.
ex.ja: トムは雨で全身びしょぬれになった。

ex.en: Tom got soaked and caught a cold.
ex.ja: トムはずぶ濡れになって、風邪をひいた。

ex.en: We were soaked to the skin but very happy.
ex.ja: 私たちはずぶぬれになっていたが、とっても幸せだった。

note.ja: soak（浸す）+ -ed。soak は suck（吸う）と同系。「びしょぬれの」。

en: A game similar to baseball but played with a larger and softer ball which can be thrown overhand or underhand.
The ball used to play the sport.

ex.en: Do you know how to play softball?
ex.ja: ソフトボールのやり方、知ってる？

note.ja: soft（柔らかい）+ ball。「ソフトボール」。

en: Of or pertaining to the southeast.

southeastern.ety: From Middle English *southesterne, from Old English sūþēasterne, equivalent to south + eastern.

ex.en: Croatia is in the southeastern part of Europe.
ex.ja: クロアチアはヨーロッパの東南部に位置する国である。

ex.en: Croatia is located in the southeastern part of Europe.
ex.ja: クロアチアはヨーロッパの東南部に位置する国である。

ex.en: Croatia is a country in southeastern Europe.
ex.ja: クロアチアはヨーロッパの東南部に位置する国である。

note.ja: south（南）+ east（東）+ -ern。「南東の」。

en: One who watches an event; especially, an event held outdoors.
One who observes, sees, or views something; an observer.

spectator.ety: Borrowed from Latin spectātor, from frequentative verb spectō (“watch”), from speciō (“look at”). Equivalent to spectate + -or. Doublet of speculator.

ex.en: The spectators were excited by his home run.
ex.ja: 彼のホームランは観衆を沸かせた。

ex.en: There were more spectators than I had expected.
ex.ja: 予想以上に多くの観客が来ていました。

ex.en: The judge bound the spectators to keep quiet.
ex.ja: 判事は傍聴人に静かにするよう警告した。

note.ja: spect（見る）+ ator（人）。見る人 →「観客・見物人」。

en: The act and skills of presenting stories and tales.
A fall, trip or substantial misstep.
An error or blunder.
To misstep; to walk or run clumsily; to trip or fall.
To make mistakes, to have trouble.

stumble.ety: Ultimately from Proto-Germanic *stam- (“to trip up; to stammer, stutter”), thereby related to German stumm (“mute”), Dutch stom (“dumb”). Doublet of stammer. Also related to verb in Dutch stommelen (“to walk silently”).

ex.en: Why do I always stumble through life like this?
ex.ja: どうして僕はこんな不器用な生き方しかできないんだろう。

ex.en: The kid stumbled and fell to his knees.
ex.ja: その子供は、つまずいて転んで膝を突いた。

ex.en: She walked carefully so as not to stumble over a rock.
ex.ja: 石につまづかないように彼女は注意深く歩を進めた。

note.ja: 北欧語に由来するとされる。「つまずく」→ つまずいて見つける →「偶然出くわす（stumble upon）」。

en: The property of being stupid.
An act that is stupid.

stupidity.ety: From Latin stupiditātem, accusative of Latin stupiditās, equivalent to stupid + -ity.

ex.en: Thanks to your stupidity, we lost the game.
ex.ja: 君が間抜けだったおかげで、僕たちはその試合に負けたんだ。

ex.en: Everyone is responsible for his own stupidity.
ex.ja: 誰もが自分自身の愚かさに責任がある。

ex.en: I wish you'd quit that sort of super-league stupidity.
ex.ja: そういう度を越したアホはやめて欲しいですねー。

note.ja: stupid（愚かな）+ -ity。ラテン語 stupere（呆然とする）。「愚かさ」。stupor（意識もうろう）と同じ。

en: To put an end to, especially with force, to crush, do away with; to prohibit, subdue.
To restrain or repress, such as laughter or an expression.

suppress.ety: From Latin suppressus, perfect passive participle of supprimō (“press down or under”), from sub (“under”) + premō (“press”).

ex.en: I wonder how I can suppress this feeling.
ex.ja: どうすれば、この気持を抑えられるのだろう。

ex.en: The government tried to suppress all opposition parties.
ex.ja: 政府はすべての野党を抑圧しようとした。

ex.en: The news was suppressed for the time being.
ex.ja: そのニュースは当分の間差し止めになった。

note.ja: sup（下へ）+ press（押す）。押さえつける →「鎮圧する・抑える」。

en: Touchable; able to be touched or felt; perceptible by the sense of touch.
Perceptible; able to be perceived.
A physical object; something that can be touched.
Real or concrete results.

tangible.ety: Borrowed from Middle French tangible, from Late Latin tangibilis, from Latin tangere (“to touch”)

ex.en: Show me tangible data.
ex.ja: 具体的なデータを示しなさい。

ex.en: Service economy is a useful labor that does not produce a tangible commodity.
ex.ja: サービス経済は物を生産しないが有益な労働である。

en: To slope or incline (something); to slant.
To be at an angle.
A slope or inclination.
The inclination of part of the body, such as backbone, pelvis, head, etc.

tilt.ety:
From Middle English tilte, from Old English *tyltan, *tieltan (“to be unsteady”), related to the adjective tealt (“unsteady”), from Proto-West Germanic *talt, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *del-, *dul- (“to shake, hesitate”), see also Dutch touteren (“to tremble”), North Frisian talt, tolt (“unstable, shaky”). Cognate with Icelandic tölt (“an ambling pace”).
The nominal sense of "a joust" appears around 1510, presumably derived from the barrier which separated the combatants, which suggests connection with tilt "covering". The modern transitive meaning is from 1590; the intransitive use

ex.en: The pillar tilted to the right and fell.
ex.ja: 柱は右へ傾いて倒れた。

ex.en: She stood silently, her head tilted slightly to one side.
ex.ja: 彼女はちょっと首をかしげて、黙然と立っていた。

ex.en: I tilt my head. Not the pawn, but the knight?
ex.ja: 僕は首をひねる。このポーンではなくて、こっちのナイトを・・・。

note.ja: 古英語 tealt（不安定な）から。「傾ける」。

en: Ignorable; of little significance or value.
Commonplace, ordinary.

trivial.ety:
PIE word
 *tréyes
* From Latin triviālis (“appropriate to the street-corner, commonplace, vulgar”), from trivium (“place where three roads meet”). Compare trivium, trivia.
* From the distinction between trivium (“the lower division of the liberal arts; grammar, logic and rhetoric”) and quadrivium (“the higher division of the seven liberal arts in the Middle Ages, composed of geometry, astronomy, arithmetic, and music”).

ex.en: He easily gets angry at trivial things.
ex.ja: 彼はつまらないことですぐ怒る。

ex.en: Don't worry about such a trivial problem.
ex.ja: そんなささいな問題にくよくよするなよ。

ex.en: Women talk about trivial things when talking with men.
ex.ja: 女性が男性と話すとき、彼女たちはどうでもいいことを話す。

note.ja: ラテン語 trivium（三叉路）から。tri（3）+ via（道）。「三叉路の井戸端会議の話」→「ささいな」。via と同じ。

en: A member of any of the various ethnic groups that speak the Turkic languages.
A member of a West Asian ethnic group native to Anatolia (which comprises the bulk of their modern nation-state of Türkiye).
Synonym of Turkic.
Synonym of Turkish.

Turk.ety: From Middle English Turke, Turk, from Old French Turc, from Medieval Latin Turcus, from Medieval Greek Τοῦρκος (Toûrkos), from Classical Persian تُرْک (turk), from Middle Persian [script needed] (twlk' /⁠turk⁠/), from Old Turkic 𐱅𐰇𐰼𐰜 (t²ẅr²ẅk²). See Proto-Turkic *tür(ü)k for more.

ex.en: No, I'm not a German, I'm a Turk.
ex.ja: いいえ。ドイツ人じゃなくて、トルコ人です。

ex.en: Constantinople fell to the hands of the Ottoman Turks in 1453.
ex.ja: 1453年、コンスタンティノープルはオスマン帝国の手に渡った。

ex.en: Cockburn Town is the capital of the Turks and Caicos Islands.
ex.ja: コックバーンタウンは、タークス・カイコス諸島の首都です。

note.ja: トルコ人。Turkey（トルコ）と同じ。

en: Not officially established.
Implicitly true but withheld and/or contradicted by authority.

note.ja: un（否定）+ official（公式の）。「非公式の」。

en: Something hung up or spread out to hide or protect the face, or hide an object from view; usually of gauze, crepe, or similar diaphanous …
Anything that partially obscures a clear view.
To dress in, or decorate with, a veil.
To conceal as with a veil.

veil.ety: From Middle English veil, veyl, from Anglo-Norman and Old Northern French veil (“sail, veil, shroud”) (Francien Old French voil, French voile), Latin vēlum (“cloth, covering”). Displaced Middle English scleire, scleyre, sleyre, slyre (“veil”) (compare German Schleier). Doublet of velum and voile.

ex.en: Is that a veiled threat?
ex.ja: それはいわゆる脅しですか？

note.ja: ラテン語 velum（覆い・帆）から。「ベール」。reveal（ベールを取る → 明らかにする）、revelation と同じ。

en: Capable of doing many things competently.
Having varied uses or many functions.

versatile.ety: From Latin versātilis (“turning easily”), from versātus, past participle of versō (“to turn, change”), frequentative of vertō (“to turn”).

ex.en: This seasoning is so versatile that you can put it on anything.
ex.ja: この調味料、万能すぎて何にでもかけてる。

en: The scientific study of humans, systematically describing the ethnographic, linguistic, archaeological, and evolutionary dimensions of hu…
The study of humanity in its relation to the divine, as in Christian anthropology.

anthropology.ety: From New Latin anthropologia, from Ancient Greek ἄνθρωπος (ánthrōpos, “human, mankind”) + -λογία (-logía). By surface analysis, anthropo- + -logy.

ex.en: This book deals with anthropology.
ex.ja: この本は人類学を扱っている。

ex.en: He is hailed as the father of modern anthropology.
ex.ja: 彼は現代人類学の父として熱烈な支持を受けている。

ex.en: He majors in social anthropology.
ex.ja: 彼は社会人類学を専攻している。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 anthrōpos（人間）+ logia（学）。「人類学」。philanthropy（人類愛）と同じ。

en: Any of the muscular- and elastic-walled blood vessels forming part of the circulation system by which blood is conveyed away from the hea…
A major transit corridor in a system of roads, rivers, or railway lines.

artery.ety: Late Middle English arterie, borrowing from Old French artaire and Latin artēria (“a windpipe; an artery”), from Ancient Greek ᾰ̓ρτηρῐ́ᾱ (ărtērĭ́ā, “windpipe; artery”).

ex.en: Lungs, heart, veins, arteries and capillaries form the cardiovascular system.
ex.ja: 肺、心臓、静脈、動脈、毛細血管により循環器系が形成されています。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 artēria（気管・動脈）から。昔は動脈が空気を運ぶと考えられた。「動脈」→「幹線道路」。

Wood of the bamboo plant as a material for building, furniture, etc.
Made of the wood of the bamboo.
To flog with a bamboo cane.
To paint (furniture, etc.) to give it the appearance of bamboo.

ex.en: The bamboo gave but did not break.
ex.ja: その竹はしなったが折れなかった。

ex.en: There's bamboo growing in the garden.
ex.ja: 庭に竹が生えている。

note.ja: マレー語 bambu から、オランダ語を経た語。「竹」。

The leaves of this plant used as a herb.
To grind the edge of a tool to an acute angle.

en: A fruit-bearing shrub of the aggregate species Rubus fruticosus and some hybrids.

To gather or forage for blackberries.

ex.en: I wonder where Tom found these blackberries.
ex.ja: トムはこのブラックベリー、どこで見つけたのかしら。

ex.en: I really like blackberries.
ex.ja: ブラックベリーが大好きなんだ。

ex.en: Tom has a Blackberry.
ex.ja: トムはBlackBerryを持ってるんだ。

note.ja: black（黒い）+ berry（実）。「ブラックベリー」。

en: Any alcoholic beverage.
Any hard liquor.

booze.ety: Originally a Northern England dialectal form of bowse.

ex.en: My friends were so boozed up that I had to drive them home.
ex.ja: 僕の友達はひどく酔っていたので、家まで車で送るはめになったんだ。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 būsen（大酒を飲む）から。

en: Diameter of the bore of a firearm, typically measured between opposite lands.
The diameter of round or cylindrical body, as of a bullet, a projectile, or a column.

ex.ja: 「状況報告を」「現在目標は目視４。最大７か。小口径火器を所有」

en: To make a call to (someone) on a cellphone.

ex.en: I threw away my cellphone into the river.
ex.ja: 川に携帯電話を投げ捨てた。

ex.en: Come on, tell me your cellphone email address.
ex.ja: ねえ、携帯のメアド教えて。

ex.en: Please don't look at your cellphone while we're eating.
ex.ja: 食事中に携帯を見るのやめなさい。

note.ja: cellular（細胞状の：基地局が蜂の巣状に並ぶ）+ phone。cell と同じ。

A line segment between two points of a curve.
To write chords for.
To accord; to harmonize together.

ex.ja: その名にどこか聞き覚えがあった。

ex.ja: 彼女のＣＤの歌詞カードにはいつもウクレレのコードが載っている。

en: A concessions stand.

ex.en: We solved the problem by mutual concessions.
ex.ja: お互い歩み寄って問題を解決した。

en: Of or pertaining to the body, especially the human body; bodily.
Pertaining to the body (the thorax and abdomen), as distinguished from the head, limbs and wings, etc.
A non-commissioned officer army rank with NATO code OR-4. The rank below a sergeant but above a lance corporal and private.
A non-commissioned officer rank in the police force, below a sergeant but above a private or patrolman.

corporal.ety: From Middle English corporal, corporall, corporel, corporell, from Old French corporal (French corporel), from Latin corporālis, from Latin corpus (“body”); compare corporeal.

ex.ja: 世論の趨勢は体罰反対の方向である。

ex.ja: 個人的には体罰は必要悪だと思っています。

ex.ja: 私は体罰には断固反対です。

en: An area, open to the sky, partially or wholly surrounded by walls or buildings.

note.ja: court（中庭）+ yard（囲い地）。「中庭」。

A tuft, or other natural ornament, growing on an animal's head, for example the comb of a cockerel, the swelling on the head of a snake, …

To reach the crest of (e.g. a hill or mountain).

crest.ety:
From Middle English creste, from Old French creste (modern French crête) and perhaps continuing Old English cræsta (“crest, tuft, plume”); both ultimately from Vulgar Latin *cresta, from Latin crista. Doublet of crista.

ex.en: I've forgotten. Was House Lancaster's family crest a red rose, or a white rose?
ex.ja: ランカスター家の紋章が赤バラだったか、白バラだったか忘れてしまった。

note.ja: ラテン語 crista（とさか）から。「とさか」→「頂上・紋章」。

en: An instance of actions and/or schemes fabricated to mislead someone into believing a lie or inaccuracy.

deception.ety: From Middle English decepcioun, from Old French decepcion, from Latin dēcipiō (“to deceive”).

note.ja: de（離れて）+ cept（取る）+ ion。（人の判断を）つかんで離さないこと →「だますこと・欺き」。deceive（だます）。

ex.ja: 車道の向こう側にあるバリケードは、「入れない」ということである。

To engage in a battle.

ex.ja: 姉妹はやっきになって言い争った。

ex.ja: 西園寺は決闘に勝つと思っていたのに負けた。

note.ja: ラテン語 duellum（戦争）、bellum の古い形。duo（2人）と結びついて「2人の戦い」→「決闘」。

ex.ja: メアリーは妖精なの。

ex.ja: 妖精たちはサンタの小さな助っ人です。

In a fair manner of distribution, giving the same amount or number to each; equally.

ex.ja: そのお金は彼ら二人で平等に分けられるでしょう。

The state of being exempt; immunity.

exemption.ety: From Old French exemption, from Latin exemptiō, from eximō, equivalent to exempt + -ion.

ex.en: You have a personal tax exemption of 500,000 yen.
ex.ja: ５０万円の個人基礎控除がある。

ex.en: We give foreign tourists the privilege of tax exemption.
ex.ja: 外国人旅行者には免税の特権がある。

ex.en: Let's take advantage of the 'exemption' controversy to reconsider the way we work.
ex.ja: 「エグゼンプション」の議論を機に働き方を見直そう。

A fashionable person; a fop.

ex.ja: かくて、国際化は日本人にとって今はやりのスローガンになっている。

ex.ja: 彼は自分の犬に新聞を取ってくるように訓練した。

ex.ja: 何か、全部、こじつけって感じがするんだけど・・・。

ex.ja: 隣の部屋から椅子を持って来て下さい。

ex.ja: その漁師達は網を海に投げた。

note.ja: fisher + man。「漁師・釣り人」。

en: Causing fear, dread, awe, or discouragement as a result of size, strength, or some other impressive feature; commanding respect; causing …
Difficult to defeat or overcome.

formidable.ety: From Middle English formidable, from Old French formidable, formible, from Latin formīdābilis (“formidable, terrible”) (whence -able), from formīdō (“fear, dread”).

ex.en: Formidable looking spiders do not attack people.
ex.ja: 見かけの恐ろしいクモは人を攻撃することはない。

supplied with furniture

Vague or imprecise.
A very small piece of plush material such as lint.
Something covered with fuzz or hair, as an animal or plush toy.

fuzzy.ety: Uncertain. Apparently from fuzz + -y, though some sources suggest that fuzz derives from fuzzy. Compare fozy, or Low German fussig (“loose; spongy”).

ex.ja: 写真がボケてる。

To use grenade(s) upon.

ex.ja: 警官隊がデモ隊に多数の催涙弾を投げた。

ex.ja: 兵士から5メートル離れてグレネードが爆発した。

note.ja: high（高い）+ lands（土地）。「高地」。the Highlands はスコットランド北部。
human resources（人的資源）の略。「人事（部）」。

en: Greatly; to a huge extent.

hugely.ety: From Middle English hugely, hugeliche, equivalent to huge + -ly.

en: The contrivance of a false appearance of virtue or goodness, while concealing real character or inclinations, especially with respect to …
The claim or pretense of having beliefs, standards, qualities, behaviours, virtues, motivations, etc. which one does not really have.

hypocrisy.ety:
From hypo- + Ancient Greek κρί(σις) (krí(sis)) + -isy. From Middle English ipocrisie, from Old French ypocrisie, from Late Latin hypocrisis, from Ancient Greek ὑπόκρισις (hupókrisis, “answer, stage acting, pretense”), from ὑποκρίνομαι (hupokrínomai, “I answer (a fellow actor on stage), play a part, dissemble, feign”), from ὑπό (hupó, “under, equivalent of the modern "hypo-" prefix”) + the middle voice of κρίνω (krínō, “I separate, judge, decide”) + -isy.
Displaced native Old English līċettung.

ex.en: We tend to associate politicians with hypocrisy.
ex.ja: 私たちは政治家というと偽善を連想しがちだ。

ex.en: They dismissed his criticism as hypocrisy.
ex.ja: 彼らは彼の批判を偽善であるとして退けた。

ex.en: Hypocrisy is the homage that vice pays to virtue.
ex.ja: 偽善とは悪徳が徳に対して払う忠順の誓いである。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 hypokrisis（役を演じること）から。hypo（下で）+ krinein（判断する）。「仮面の下で演じること」→「偽善」。

en: Mistaken or incorrect; not accurate.

inaccurate.ety: From in- + accurate. See also unaccurate.

ex.en: The wall clock of the living room is inaccurate.
ex.ja: リビングの掛け時計は狂ってるよ。

ex.en: Our experiment has revealed that his report was inaccurate.
ex.ja: 我々の実験の結果、彼の報告は不正確なことがわかった。

ex.en: The data is often inaccurate.
ex.ja: データはしばしば不正確だ。

en: The creation or beginning of something; the establishment.
A layering, nesting, or recursion of something within itself.

inception.ety:
Late Middle English, borrowed from Latin inceptiō, from inceptus, perfect passive participle of incipiō (“to begin”).
The layering sense derives from the 2010 science fiction film Inception, in which a team of people infiltrate someone’s subconscious mind, proceeding through several layers of dreams with the goal of causing the target to incept an idea.

en: Lacking the degree of ability and responsibility necessary to do a task successfully.
Unable to make rational decisions; insane or otherwise cognitively impaired.
A person who is incompetent.

incompetent.ety: Borrowed from French incompétent, from Late Latin incompetentem, from Latin incompetēns, equivalent to in- + competent.

ex.en: The world is full of incompetent doctors.
ex.ja: 世の中は藪医者だらけ。

note.ja: in（否定）+ competent（有能な）。ラテン語 competere（ふさわしい）。「無能な」。

en: In a manner that is not definite.
For a long time, with no defined end.

indefinitely.ety:
Etymology tree
English indefinite
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English indefinitely
From indefinite + -ly.

ex.ja: 宇宙は無限に膨張し続けるのか？

ex.en: The game has been postponed indefinitely.
ex.ja: ゲームは無期延期になった。

ex.en: The game has been indefinitely postponed.
ex.ja: ゲームは無期延期になった。

note.ja: in（否定）+ definite（明確な）+ -ly。「期限を定めずに」→「無期限に」。

en: To become involved in a situation, so as to alter or prevent an action.
To occur, fall, or come between, points of time, or events.

intervene.ety: Back-formation from intervention, and/or from Latin interveniō (“come between”, verb).

ex.en: We take health for granted until illness intervenes.
ex.ja: 病気になるまで、我々は健康を当たり前のものだと思っている。

ex.en: That country intervened in the internal affairs of our nation.
ex.ja: その国はわが国に内政干渉をした。

ex.en: They should not intervene in the internal affairs of another country.
ex.ja: 彼らは他国の内政に干渉すべきではない。

en: Race; family; breed; kind.
Persons of the same race or family; kindred.
Related by blood or marriage, akin. (It is more common to form sentences using the noun instead.)

kin.ety:
From Middle English kyn, from Old English cynn (“kind, sort, rank”), from Proto-West Germanic *kuni, from Proto-Germanic *kunją (“race, generation, descent”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵn̥h₁yom, from *ǵenh₁- (“to produce”).
Cognate with Scots kin (“relatives, kinfolk”), North Frisian kinn, kenn (“gender, race, family, kinship”), Dutch kunne (“gender, sex”), Middle Low German kunne (“gender, sex, race, family, lineage”), Danish køn (“gender, sex”), Norwegian Bokmål and Norwegian Nynorsk kjønn (“gender, sex”), Swedish kön (“gender, sex”), Faroese and Icelandic kyn (“gender”), Finnish kunnia (“ho

ex.en: They are of kin to each other.
ex.ja: 彼らは互いに親類関係にある。

note.ja: 古英語 cynn（一族）から。kind（種類・親切な）、king（一族の長）と同じ祖先。「親族」。

en: especially a member of a legislative body.
especially not any individual member of a legislative body but the abstracted author of a statute or statutes relevant for the principles…

ex.en: The legislators of that state did away with outdated laws.
ex.ja: その州の立法者は時代遅れの法律を廃止した。

ex.en: Legislators in the Diet are struggling to find a solution to the problem.
ex.ja: 国会議員は問題の解決に苦慮しています。

note.ja: ラテン語 legis lator（法を持ち込む人）。lex（法）+ lator（運ぶ人）。「立法者」。legislation と同じ。

en: A crustacean of the Nephropidae family, dark green or blue-black in colour turning bright red when cooked, with a hard shell and claws, w…
A spiny lobster, also called the rock lobster, a crustacean of the Palinuridae family, pinkish red in colour, with a hard, spiny shell bu…
To fish for lobsters.
Red-colored, especially from a sunburn.

lobster.ety:
Etymology tree
Old English loppestre
Middle English loppestere
English lobster
From Middle English loppestere, lopster, from Old English loppestre, lopustre, lopystre, of uncertain origin. Some believe it to be a corruption of Latin lō̆custa (“grasshopper, locust”) + the Old English feminine agent suffix -estre. In Latin, the phrase lō̆custa marīna (literally "sea-grasshopper") signified a type of crustacean (shrimp or lobster).
Alternatively, from Old English lobbe, loppe (“spider”) + the Old English feminine agent suffix -estre, equivalent to lop + -ster.

ex.en: Lobsters belong to a class of marine animals.
ex.ja: ロブスターは海洋動物の一種に属します。

ex.en: I don't want to eat a live lobster.
ex.ja: 私は生きたままのえびは食べたくない。

ex.en: I want to eat lobster again tonight.
ex.ja: 今日の夜はまたロブスターが食べたいなあ。

note.ja: 古英語 loppestre から。ラテン語 locusta（イナゴ・エビ）と、loppe（クモ）が混ざった語。locust（イナゴ）と同じ語源。

en: A feeling of depression resulting from being alone or from having no companions.
The condition or state of being alone or having no companions.

ex.en: Life has a loneliness one cannot truly understand until reaching old age.
ex.ja: 人生には老年にならぬと解らない淋しい気持があるものだ。

ex.en: Sometimes I have feelings of being tormented by loneliness.
ex.ja: 時々、孤独感に苛まれることがあります。

ex.en: Guinea pigs can die of loneliness.
ex.ja: モルモットは孤独死しちゃうんだ。

note.ja: lonely（寂しい）+ -ness。lone は alone の短縮。「孤独」。

en: A disease spread by mosquito, in which a protozoan, Plasmodium, multiplies in blood every few days.

malaria.ety: Borrowed from Italian malaria, formed from mal- (“bad”) and aria (“air”). Introduced into English by the Scottish geologist John MacCulloch (1773–1835). Displaced native Old English unlyft (literally “bad air”).

ex.en: Malaria is a disease that mosquitoes carry.
ex.ja: マラリアは蚊が運ぶ病気です。

ex.en: Malaria is carried by mosquitoes.
ex.ja: マラリアは蚊が媒介する。

ex.en: He contracted malaria while living in the jungle.
ex.ja: 彼はジャングルに住んでいる間にマラリアにかかった。

note.ja: イタリア語 mala aria（悪い空気）から。沼地の悪い空気が原因と考えられたことから。

en: A public declaration of principles, policies, or intentions, especially that of a political party.
To issue a manifesto.

manifesto.ety: Since the mid 17th century, from Italian manifesto, from manifestare + -o, from Latin manifestō (“to make public”), from Latin manus + an uncertain second element. Doublet of manifest.

note.ja: イタリア語 manifesto（明らかにすること）から。manifest と同じ。「宣言・マニフェスト」。

en: A labyrinth; a puzzle consisting of a complicated network of paths or passages, the aim of which is to find one's way through.
Something made up of many confused or conflicting elements; a tangle.

maze.ety: From Middle English mase, from Middle English masen (“to perplex, bewilder”); or perhaps from Old English *mæs (“delusion, bewilderment”); akin to Old English āmasian (“to perplex, confound”), Icelandic masa (“to chatter”). More at amaze.

ex.en: This maze is very hard to get out of.
ex.ja: この迷路は抜け出すのがとても難しい。

ex.en: Yesterday we went into a huge maze.
ex.ja: 昨日大きな迷路に入りました。

ex.en: The boy could not find his way out of the maze.
ex.ja: 少年は迷路から抜け出せなかった。

note.ja: amaze（呆然とさせる）と同じ語。「頭を混乱させるもの」→「迷路」。

en: A residence for monks or others who have taken religious vows.

monastery.ety: From Middle English monasterie, from Old French monastere, from Medieval Latin monastērium (“monastery”), from Ancient Greek μοναστήριον (monastḗrion, “hermitage, monastery”), from μοναστήριος (monastḗrios, “alone, made alone”) + -ιον (-ion, “-ium”, suffix forming place names), from μονάζω (monázō, “to be alone”), from μόνος (mónos, “alone”) + -άζω (-ázō, verb-forming suffix). Doublet of minster.

ex.en: Monks used to play tennis in monasteries.
ex.ja: 当時は修道僧達が修道院でよくテニスをしていた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 monastērion から。monazein（ひとりで暮らす）、monos。「修道院」。monk と同じ。

en: Any alteration or change.
Any heritable change of the base-pair sequence of genetic material.

mutation.ety: Late 14th century as Middle English mutacioun, from Latin mūtātiō, both directly and via Old French mutacion.

ex.en: Without the random mutation of genes there would be no evolution.
ex.ja: 遺伝子の突然変異がなければ、進化は起こりえない。

ex.en: White strawberries were born of a mutation during selective breeding.
ex.ja: 白いちごは、品種改良中の突然変異によって生まれました。

note.ja: mut（変える）+ ation。変わること →「突然変異・変化」。

en: In a narrow manner; without flexibility or latitude.
Closely; by a narrow margin.

narrowly.ety: From Middle English narowly, equivalent to narrow + -ly.

ex.en: The federal budget was narrowly approved by Congress.
ex.ja: 連邦予算はかろうじて議会の承認を得た。

ex.en: The budget was narrowly approved by Congress.
ex.ja: 予算はかろうじて議会の承認を得た。

ex.en: I narrowly escaped being hit by a car.
ex.ja: かろうじて車に当てられずにすんだ。

note.ja: narrow（狭い）+ -ly。「狭く」→ ぎりぎりで →「かろうじて」。

en: The state of being negligent.
The tort whereby a duty of reasonable care was breached, causing damage: any conduct short of intentional or reckless action that falls b…

negligence.ety: From Middle English necligence, negligence, from Old French negligence, from Latin neglegentia.

ex.en: This failure was brought about by your own negligence.
ex.ja: この失敗は、君自身の怠慢から起こったものだ。

ex.en: The accident happened because of the driver's negligence.
ex.ja: その事故は運転手の不注意から起きた。

ex.en: The accident was due to the negligence of the caretaker.
ex.ja: その事故の責任は管理人の怠慢にある。

note.ja: neglect（怠る）と同じ語源。ラテン語 neglegere ＝ neg（否定）+ legere（選ぶ・拾う）。「拾わない」→「怠慢・過失」。

en: A form or state of connection.
The relationship between a vendor and a jurisdiction for the purpose of taxation, established for example by the vendor operating a physi…

note.ja: ラテン語 nexus（結びつき）から。nectere（結ぶ）。connect と同じ。

en: A public or private establishment that is open late at night to provide entertainment, food, drink, music or dancing.
A strip club.
To visit a nightclub (or nightclubs) for entertainment.

ex.ja: フラメンコを踊るナイトクラブもある。

ex.en: The tourists were ripped off at the nightclub.
ex.ja: 旅行者は、そのナイトクラブでむしり取られた。

note.ja: night（夜）+ club（クラブ）。「ナイトクラブ」。

Imperfectly developed; not very distinct.
To cause to become obsolete.
An obsolete thing or person.

en: Of, or relating to the eye or to vision.
Of, or relating to optics or optical instruments.
A lens or other part of an optical instrument that interacts with light.
A measuring device with a small window, attached to an upside-down bottle, used to dispense alcoholic drinks in a bar.

optic.ety: Borrowed from Middle French optique or Medieval Latin opticus, from Ancient Greek ὀπτῐκός (optĭkós, “of or for sight”), from ὀπτός (optós, “visible”) + -ῐκός (-ĭkós, “-ic”, adjectival suffix).

ex.en: Fibre-optic cables can carry huge amounts of information.
ex.ja: 光ファイバーケーブルは膨大な量の情報を搬送できる。

ex.en: His study of optics led him to the invention of the magnifying glass.
ex.ja: 光学の研究で彼は拡大鏡の発明をした。

en: A brahmin who acts as the hereditary superintendent of a particular ghat or temple, and is regarded as knowledgeable in matters of geneal…

panda.ety:
Borrowed from French panda, of unclear ultimate origin but probably from the second element of nigálya-pónya, a local name for the red panda recorded in Nepal and Sikkim by Brian Houghton Hodgson (1800 or 1801 – 1894), an ethnologist, naturalist and the British Resident of Nepal, possibly from Nepali निँगाले (nĩgāle, “relating to a certain species of bamboo”) (the adjectival form of निँगालो (nĩgālo), a variant of निङालो (niṅālo, “Drepanostachyum intermedium, a species of bamboo”)) + a regional Tibetan name for the animal (compare regional Tibetan ཕོ་ཉ (pho nya, “messenger”)).

ex.en: Do you mean that you've never seen a panda?
ex.ja: パンダを一度も見たことがないって言ってる？

ex.en: He says he's never seen a panda.
ex.ja: パンダ見たことないんだって。

ex.en: I had never seen a panda till that time.
ex.ja: 私は、その時まで、パンダを見たことはなかった。

note.ja: ネパール語に由来するとされる。もとはレッサーパンダを指した。

en: Any of certain plants of the family Fabaceae: Pisum sativum and others.
A plant, Pisum sativum, member of the legume (Fabaceae) family.

ex.en: The two brothers are as like as two peas.
ex.ja: その二人の兄弟はうり二つである。

ex.en: I'm sick of eating peas.
ex.ja: グリンピースはもううんざりなんだ。

ex.en: Go buy some green peas — the frozen kind.
ex.ja: グリンピース買ってきて。冷凍のやつね。

note.ja: pease（豆）が複数形と誤解されて s が取れた語。ラテン語 pisum。「エンドウ豆」。

en: The way a person holds and positions their body.
A situation or condition.
To put one's body into a posture or series of postures, especially hoping that one will be noticed and admired.
To pretend to have an opinion or a conviction.

posture.ety: Borrowed from Middle French posture, from Italian postura, from Latin positūra (“position, situation”). Doublet of positura.

ex.en: Use good posture while eating.
ex.ja: 犬食いはみっともないよね。

ex.en: He likes to posture as an intellectual.
ex.ja: 彼は知識人ぶるのが好きだ。

note.ja: pos（置く）+ ture。体の置き方 →「姿勢・態度」。

en: The period before the start of a sporting season, during which players undergo training and venues are prepared
To season in advance.

ex.en: He was doing really well in the preseason, but that was it.
ex.ja: オープン戦だけ絶好調だった。

note.ja: pre（前の）+ season（シーズン）。「シーズン前」。

en: To renew or revitalize.
To become fresh again; to be revitalized.
The periodic energizing required to maintain the contents of computer memory, the display luminance of a computer screen, etc.
The update of a display (in a web browser or similar software) to show the latest version of the data.

refresh.ety: From Middle English refreshen, refreschen, refrisschen, from Old French refrescher (“to refresh”) (modern French rafraîchir), equivalent to re- + fresh.

ex.en: He refreshed himself with a cup of tea.
ex.ja: お茶を一杯飲んで彼は元気が出た。

ex.en: She refreshed her memory with the photo.
ex.ja: 彼女はその写真を見ると記憶がよみがえってきた。

ex.en: A glass of orange juice refreshed me.
ex.ja: オレンジジュースを飲んだら気分がさわやかになった。

en: The quality of being resonant.
A resonant sound, echo, or reverberation, such as that produced by blowing over the top of a bottle.

resonance.ety: From Old French resonance (French résonance), from Latin resonantia (“echo”), from resonō (“to resound”).

ex.en: By using four types of metal, specific frequency resonance is suppressed.
ex.ja: 四種類の金属を使うことで特定の共振を抑えます。

note.ja: resonate（共鳴する）+ -ance。re（再び）+ sonare（鳴る）。「鳴り返すこと」→「共鳴・反響」。sound、sonic と同じ son。

Uncompromising; unrelenting.

The ship, crew or cargo so rescued.
To rescue.
To modify (a false proposition) to create a true proposition.

en: In feudal Japan, a soldier who served a daimyo.

ex.en: I live by the way of the samurai.
ex.ja: 俺は侍の道で生きてる。

ex.ja: 現代の日本に忍者や侍はいません。

en: A literary device of writing or art which principally ridicules its subject often as an intended means of provoking or preventing change …
A satirical work.

satire.ety: From Middle French satire, from Old French, from Latin satira, from earlier satura, from lanx satura (“full dish”), from feminine of satur. Altered in Latin by influence of Ancient Greek σάτυρος (sáturos, “satyr”), on the mistaken notion that the form is related to the Greek σατυρικὸν δράμα (saturikòn dráma, “satyr drama”).

ex.en: The play is a satire on the political world.
ex.ja: その劇は政界を風刺したものだ。

ex.en: He was not aware that the praise was a satire in disguise.
ex.ja: その賞賛は皮肉の変装したものであることに彼は気がつかなかった。

note.ja: ラテン語 satura（いろいろ盛った皿・ごった煮）から。「ごった煮の詩」→「風刺」。

en: Food from the sea, including that derived from fish, shellfish, crustaceans, cephalopods, seaweed, algae, marine mammals, and other marin…
Food from any aquatic source, including not only salt water but also fresh water.

ex.en: I really like eating seafood.
ex.ja: 私は海産物を食べるのが大好きだ。

ex.en: I like seafood a lot.
ex.ja: シーフード、めちゃ好きよ。

ex.en: This is by far the best seafood restaurant in this area.
ex.ja: ここは、この地域では飛び抜けて最高のシーフードレストランだ。

note.ja: sea（海）+ food（食べ物）。「魚介類」。

en: A swift, broad cutting stroke, especially one made with an edged weapon or whip.
A wide striking motion made with an implement such as a cricket bat, hockey stick, or lacrosse stick.
To cut with a swift broad stroke of an edged weapon.
To produce a similar wound with a savage strike of a whip.
Used to note the sound or action of a slash.
Used to connect two or more identities in a list.
Used to list alternatives.

slash.ety:
Late Middle English, originally a verb of uncertain etymology. Perhaps of imitative origin, or possibly from Old French esclachier (“to break in pieces”), a variant of esclater, which is likely a Germanic borrowing, from Frankish *slaitan (“to slit, tear”).
Used in the Wycliffe Bible as slascht (see 1 Kings 5:18) but otherwise unattested until 16th century. Conjunctive use from various applications of the punctuation mark ⟨/⟩. See also slash fiction.

ex.en: The Federal Reserve slashed interest rates.
ex.ja: 米国連邦準備銀行は金利を引き下げました。

ex.en: Japanese corporations are slashing their capital spending programs.
ex.ja: 日本の企業はいま投資支出計画を削減している。

note.ja: 中英語 slaschen から。擬音的な語。「切りつける」→ 大胆に削る →「大幅に削減する」、切り傷のような線 →「斜線」。

en: A type of pasta made in the shape of long thin strings.
A dish that has spaghetti (noun 1 sense 1) as a main part of it, such as spaghetti bolognese.
To serve (someone) spaghetti (noun noun 1 sense 1).
To cause (someone or something) to become, or appear to become, longer and thinner; to stretch.

Spago is derived from Latin spagus (“twine”), probably from Ancient Greek σφάκος (sphákos, “apple sage (Salvia pomifera)”), probably from Pre-Greek. The verb is derived from the noun.

ex.en: I'm pretty good at cooking spaghetti.
ex.ja: 私、パスタ料理がすごく得意なの。

ex.en: You have some spaghetti sauce on your face.
ex.ja: 顔にスパゲッティーのソースがついているよ。

ex.en: At this restaurant, you eat spaghetti with chopsticks.
ex.ja: このお店ではスパゲッティをお箸でいただくんです。

note.ja: イタリア語 spaghetto（細いひも）の複数形。spago（ひも）+ 縮小。

en: Proceeding with or characterized by high speed; rapid.
To process in a faster than normal, accelerated way.
To apply the speedy rule in an online community (often the deletion rule); to speedy delete.

speedy.ety: From Middle English spedy, spedi, from Old English spēdiġ (“having good speed, lucky, prosperous; having means, wealthy, opulent, rich in material wealth; rich in, abounding in, abundant, plenteous, copious; powerful”), from Proto-West Germanic *spōdīg (“successful, hurried”), equivalent to speed + -y. Cognate with Scots speedy (“speedy”), West Frisian spoedich (“speedily, quickly, soon”), Dutch spoedig (“speedy, swift, rapid, quick”), Low German spoodig, spödig (“hasty, fast, swift, quick”), German sputig, spudig (“industrious, speedy”).

ex.en: I wish your father a speedy recovery.
ex.ja: お父さんが早く良くなりますように。

ex.en: The doctor's quick arrival brought about her very speedy recovery.
ex.ja: 医者がすぐ来てくれたので、彼女は早く回復した。

ex.en: The doctor's careful examination of the patient brought about his speedy recovery.
ex.ja: 医者が患者を丹念に診察したおかげで、患者はどんどんよくなった。

note.ja: speed（速さ）+ -y。「迅速な」。

en: A point of view; a perspective.

standpoint.ety: From stand + point, a calque of German Standpunkt. Similar constructions used in other languages, such as Japanese 立場 (tachiba, literally “standing place”).

ex.en: We can consider the problem from several standpoints.
ex.ja: いろいろな観点からその問題を検討できる。

ex.en: From the standpoint of the law, he is free.
ex.ja: 法律の観点からすると、彼は自由だ。

ex.en: From this standpoint history can be divided into two main epochs.
ex.ja: この見地から歴史は２つの主要な時期に分けられる。

note.ja: stand（立つ）+ point（地点）。ドイツ語 Standpunkt のなぞり。「立つ位置」→「観点・立場」。

en: The act of swaying; a swaying motion; a swing or sweep of a weapon.
A rocking or swinging motion.
To move or swing from side to side; or backward and forward; to rock.
To move or wield with the hand; to swing; to wield.

sway.ety:
From earlier swey (“to fall, swoon”), from Middle English sweyen, from Old English *swǣġan (“to bend, bow”), from Proto-West Germanic *swaigijan, from Proto-Germanic *swaigijaną, from Proto-Indo-European *sweh₁-
See also Saterland Frisian swooie (“to swing, wave, wobble”); also Lithuanian svai̇̃gti (“to become giddy or dizzy”), the second element of Avestan 𐬞𐬀𐬌𐬭𐬌-𐬱𐬑𐬎𐬀𐬑𐬙𐬀 (paⁱri-šxuaxta, “to surround”), Sanskrit स्वजते (svájate, “he embraces, enfolds”).
The noun derived from the verb.

ex.en: Tall buildings may sway in a strong wind.
ex.ja: 強風が吹けば高層ビルは揺れるだろう。

ex.en: He has never swayed from his duty.
ex.ja: 彼は自分の本分を踏み外したことがない。

ex.en: The ship swayed in the strong wind.
ex.ja: 船は強い風を受けて揺れた。

note.ja: 北欧語 sveigja（曲げる）から。「揺れる・揺さぶる」→「左右する」。

en: To end something, especially when left in an incomplete state.
To conclude.
Terminated; limited; bounded; ended.
Having a definite and clear limit or boundary; having a determinate size, shape or magnitude.

terminate.ety: From Middle English terminaten (“to bring to an end; to adjudicate; to end, stop; to border, confine, contain”) from terminat(e) (“bounded”, also used as the past participle of terminaten) + -en (verb-forming suffix), borrowed from Latin terminātus, perfect passive participle of terminō (“to set bounds to, bound, limit, end, close, terminate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from terminus (“a bound, limit, end”) + -ō (verb-forming suffix); see term, terminus. Doublet of termine, cognate with French terminer.

ex.en: The Tokaido line terminates at Tokyo.
ex.ja: 東海道線は東京が終点だ。

note.ja: termin（境界・終わり）+ ate。終わりにする →「終わらせる・解雇する」。

en: A rotational or twisting effect of a force; a moment of force, defined for measurement purposes as an equivalent straight line force mult…
To make something rotate about an axis by imparting torque to it.

note.ja: ラテン語 torquere（ねじる）から。ねじる力 →「トルク・回転力」。torture（拷問）も同じ。

en: An unoccupied position or job.
An available room in a hotel; guest house, etc.

vacancy.ety: From Late Latin vacantia. Doublet of vacance.

ex.ja: 彼の辞職で官僚の席に空きができた。

en: A political right to disapprove of (and thereby stop) the process of a decision, a law etc.
An invocation of that right.
To use a veto against.
To countermand.

ex.en: The President vetoed the bill, but Congress overrode his veto.
ex.ja: 大統領はその法案に対して拒否権を行使しましたが、議会が再度それを無効にしました。

note.ja: ラテン語で「私は禁じる」。vetare（禁じる）。古代ローマの護民官が使った言葉から「拒否権」。

en: A small door or gate, especially one beside a larger one.
A small window or other opening, sometimes fitted with a grating.

wicket.ety: From Middle English wiket, from Anglo-Norman and Old Northern French wiket, from Old East Old Norse víkjask (“to move oneself, move around”), reflexive of víkja, víkva, ýkva (“to yield, turn, move, go”), from Proto-Germanic *wīkwaną (“to yield, bend, turn”). note.ja: 古フランス語 wiket（小さな門）から。

en: To resist or endure (something) successfully.
To oppose (something) forcefully.

withstand.ety: From Middle English withstanden, from Old English wiþstandan, from Proto-West Germanic *wiþistandan (“to withstand, resist”), equivalent to with- (“against”) + stand. Cognate with Old Frisian withstanda (“to resist”). Compare also Dutch weerstaan (“to withstand, repel”), German widerstehen (“to withstand, resist, defy”), Russian противостоять (protivostojatʹ, “to withstand”).

ex.en: My house is designed to withstand an earthquake.
ex.ja: 私の家は地震に堪えるように設計されている。

ex.en: My house is designed so as to withstand an earthquake.
ex.ja: 私の家は地震に堪えるように設計されている。

ex.en: Robots can withstand dangerous conditions.
ex.ja: ロボットなら危険な状態になっても切り抜けられる。

note.ja: with（逆らって）+ stand（立つ）。「逆らって立つ」→「耐える」。withdraw、withhold と同じ with（逆らって・離れて）。

en: Of a creature or object: growing, living, or existing in a woodland.
Land covered with woody vegetation.
A low-density forest.

woodland.ety:
From Middle English wodeland, wodelond, from Old English wuduland (“woodland; forestland; forest”), equivalent to wood + land. Compare West Frisian wâldlân, Dutch bosland, German Waldland, Icelandic skóglendi.
Eclipsed non-native Middle English salt (“woodland”), borrowed from Latin saltus (“woodland, forest”).

ex.en: The woodland was parceled into farms.
ex.ja: 森林地はいくつかの農場に分けられた。

note.ja: wood（森）+ land（土地）。「森林地帯」。

An atom of this element.

ex.ja: この金属は亜鉛と呼ばれる。

en: Familiar with something through repeated experience; adapted to existing conditions. (of a person)
Familiar through use; usual; customary. (of a thing, condition, activity, etc.)

ex.en: I am not accustomed to speaking in public.
ex.ja: 人前で話すことに慣れていないの。

ex.en: You'll soon get accustomed to this cold weather.
ex.ja: 君はこの寒さにすぐ慣れるだろう。

ex.en: They soon became quite accustomed to each other.
ex.ja: 彼らはお互いにすぐなじんだ。

ex.ja: 彼女のおおよその年齢しか知らない。

ex.ja: 彼の証言は真相に近い。

ex.ja: その物語は歴史的真実に近い。

en: A staff or truncheon, used for various purposes.
A ceremonial staff of a field marshal or a similar high-ranking military office.
To strike with a baton.

baton.ety: From French bâton. Doublet of baston.

ex.ja: リレー用のバトンが１本足りないんです。

note.ja: フランス語 bâton（棒）から。「指揮棒・バトン・警棒」。

en: The act of breaking up; disintegration or division.
The termination of a friendship or a romantic relationship.

ex.en: Please understand that I don't want to hear about people's breakup stories.

ex.en: I beg of you not to listen to people's breakup stories.
ex.ja: ひとの別れ話なんて聞くもんじゃないな。

note.ja: break up（ばらばらになる・別れる）の名詞化。「別れ・解体」。

en: A breed of dog developed in England by the crossing of the bullbaiting dog and the Pug to produce a ladies' companion dog, having a very …
The original form of this breed, the English bulldog.
To force oneself (in a particular direction).
To chase (a steer) on horseback and wrestle it to the ground by twisting its horns (as a rodeo performance).

bulldog.ety: From bull + dog, in reference to bullbaiting.

ex.en: Don't go near the bulldog. You wouldn't want him to bite you.
ex.ja: 噛みつくといけないのでそのブルドッグに近寄るな。

note.ja: bull（雄牛）+ dog（犬）。牛と闘わせた犬（牛いじめ）から。

en: A mammalian beast of burden, much used in desert areas, of the genus Camelus.
A light brownish color, like that of a camel (also called camel brown).
Of a light brown color like that of a camel.

ex.en: Our journey by camel was quite an experience.
ex.ja: ラクダの旅は全く素晴らしい体験だった。

ex.en: In the desert we were independent of camels.
ex.ja: その砂漠で私たちはラクダを使わなかった。

ex.en: They cannot do without camels in this country.
ex.ja: この国では、ラクダはなくてはならない。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kamēlos から。ヘブライ語 gāmāl に由来する。「ラクダ」。

en: The business of providing food and related services; foodservice.
The business of providing such services for special occasions.

ex.en: I arranged catering for tomorrow's party.
ex.ja: 明日のパーティーにはケータリングを手配しました。

note.ja: cater（料理をまかなう）+ -ing。古フランス語 acater（買う）。「食料を調達すること」→「仕出し」。

en: The process of checking out of a hotel, or the latest time to vacate a room in one.
The process of checking out items at a supermarket or library.

ex.en: When is checkout time?
ex.ja: チェックアウトは何時ですか。

ex.ja: 彼は級友と仲が良い。

An unsweetened brown powder made from roasted, ground cocoa beans, used in making chocolate, and in cooking.

cocoa.ety: From Spanish cacao, from Classical Nahuatl cacahuatl. The form cocoa came about by confusion with coco, popularized by Samuel Johnson's A Dictionary of the English Language. Doublet of cacao.

ex.ja: その国の主な産物はココアと金である。

ex.ja: ココアでもどうですか？

en: The result of having been worn away or eroded, as by a glacier on rock or the sea on a cliff face.

erosion.ety:
From Middle French erosion, from Latin ērōsiō (“eating away”), derived from ērōdō.
The first known occurrence in English was in the 1541 translation by Robert Copland of Guy de Chauliac's medical text The Questyonary of Cyrurygens. Copland used erosion to describe how ulcers developed in the mouth. By 1774 erosion was used outside medical subjects. Oliver Goldsmith employed the term in the more contemporary geological context, in his book Natural History, with the quote
: "Bounds are thus put to the erosion of the earth by water."

ex.ja: もしあの丘の木々が切り倒されたら、急速に浸食を見ることになるだろう。

note.ja: erode（浸食する）+ -sion。e（外へ）+ rodere（かじる）。「かじり取られること」→「浸食」。rodent（げっ歯類）と同じ。

en: That which has mutated, with one or more new characteristics from a mutation.
Someone or something that seems strange, abnormal, or bizarre.
Of, relating to, undergoing (i.e. mutating), or resulting from change or mutation; that has undergone mutation.
Strange, abnormal, or bizarre.

mutant.ety: From Latin mūtāns, present participle of mūtō. By surface analysis, muta- + -ant.

note.ja: mut（変える）+ ant。変化したもの →「突然変異体・ミュータント」。

en: The collection of myths of a people, concerning the origin of the people, history, deities, ancestors and heroes.
A similar body of myths concerning an event, person or institution.

mythology.ety: First attested as Middle English in 1412. From Middle French mythologie, from Latin mȳthologia, from Ancient Greek μυθολογία (muthología, “legend”) μυθολογέω (muthologéō, “to tell tales”), from μυθολόγος (muthológos, “legend”), from μῦθος (mûthos, “story”) + λέγω (légō, “to say”). By surface analysis, myth + -ology or mytho- + -logy.

ex.en: In Greek mythology, Ares was the god of war.
ex.ja: ギリシャ神話では、アレスは戦争の神でした。

ex.en: The story of a great flood is very common in world mythology.
ex.ja: 世界神話の中でも、大洪水の話はとても有名だ。

ex.en: For some reason economic booms have names taken from Japanese mythology given to them.
ex.ja: なぜか、景気の良いときには日本の神話にちなんだ名前が付けられています。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 mythos（物語）+ log（学問）+ y。神話の体系 →「神話・神話学」。

en: The chemical element (symbol Ne) with an atomic number of 10. The second of the noble gases, it is a colourless, odorless inert gas.
A form or sample of the element.
That resembles a neon light; extremely bright; fluorescent

neon.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *nu
Proto-Indo-European *néwos
Proto-Hellenic *néwos
Ancient Greek νέος (néos)
Ancient Greek νέον (néon)lbor.
English neon
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek νέον (néon), neuter of νέος (néos, “new”), from Proto-Hellenic *newos, from Proto-Indo-European *néwos. By surface analysis, neo- + -on (suffix used in all noble gases).

ex.en: Tom's fursona is a fox named Neon.
ex.ja: トムのファーソナはネオンという名前のキツネだよ。

ex.en: The neon sign shone as if to invite us.
ex.ja: 私たちを招くようにネオンサインが輝いていた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 neos（新しい）から。1898年に発見された「新しい」元素。neo-（新）と同じ。

en: Of, related to, located in, or from the northeast.

northeastern.ety: From Middle English norþesterne, from Old English norþēasterne, equivalent to north + eastern.

note.ja: north + east + -ern。「北東の」。

en: A member of a Christian religious community of women who live by certain vows and usually wear a habit, (Roman Catholicism, specifically)…
A member of a similar female community in other confessions.

nun.ety: From Middle English nonne, nunne, from Old English nunne (“nun”), from Late Latin nonna (“nun, tutor”), originally (along with masculine form nonnus (“man”)) a term of address for elderly persons, perhaps from children's speech, reminiscent of nana, like papa etc. Doublet of nonna.

ex.en: The nun prayed and crossed herself.
ex.ja: 尼僧はお祈りをして十字を切った。

ex.en: When she became a nun, she took the name Sister Teresa.
ex.ja: 修道女になったとき、シスター・テレサの名を受けた。

ex.en: She led a group of nuns called the Missionaries of Charity.
ex.ja: 彼女は慈善伝導団と呼ばれる修道女達の集団を指導していた。

note.ja: ラテン語 nonna（年配の女性・修道女）から。「修道女」。

en: A lever operated by one's foot that is used to control or power a machine or mechanism, such as a bicycle or piano.
an orthopedic structure or a footlike part.
To operate a pedal attached to a wheel in a continuous circular motion.
To operate a bicycle.
Of or relating to the foot.

ex.en: Each time you step on the pedal, the wheel turns once.
ex.ja: ペダルを踏むたびごとに、車輪が一回転する。

ex.en: I broke the clutch pedal.
ex.ja: クラッチペダルを壊してしまいました。

ex.en: Press the brake pedal to turn on your brake lights.
ex.ja: ブレーキペダルを押して、ブレーキライトをつけてみてください。

note.ja: ラテン語 pes（足）から。ped + al。足で踏むもの →「ペダル」。pedestrian（歩行者）も同じ ped。

en: Any destructive insect that attacks crops or livestock; an agricultural pest.
An annoying person, a nuisance.

pest.ety: In the 16th century in the sense of "pestilence" and specifically bubonic plague from Middle French peste (“pestilence”) (whence French peste). The other meanings are recorded soon after. Ultimately from Latin pestis.

ex.en: Get off me you little pest!
ex.ja: ベタベタするんじゃねえよっ！鬱陶しい！

ex.en: Dammit, that pest Nagisa, she really went and snitched on me to the teachers.
ex.ja: くそー、渚のやつ、本当に先生にチクりやがった。

note.ja: ラテン語 pestis（疫病）から。「疫病」→「害虫・厄介者」。pesticide（殺虫剤）、plague の類語。

en: A large post, often used as supporting architecture.
Something resembling such a structure.
To provide with pillars or added strength as if from pillars.

pillar.ety: From Middle English piler, from Old French pilier, from Medieval Latin or Vulgar Latin *pilāre (“a pillar”), from Latin pila (“a pillar, pier, mole”). Displaced native Old English sweor (“pillar, column”) and Old English stapol.

ex.en: There was a knife stuck in the pillar.
ex.ja: 柱にナイフが突き刺さっていた。

ex.en: These pillars are made of stone.
ex.ja: これは石柱である。

ex.en: These pillars support the stage.
ex.ja: これらの柱が舞台を支えています。

note.ja: ラテン語 pila（柱）から。「柱」→ 組織を支える人 →「中心人物」。pile（杭）と同系。

en: Seemingly or apparently valid, likely, or acceptable; conceivably true or likely.
Obtaining approbation; specifically pleasing; apparently right; specious.

plausible.ety: From Latin plausibilis (“deserving applause, praiseworthy, acceptable, pleasing”), from the participle stem of plaudere (“to applaud”).

ex.en: Your explanation sounds plausible, but it just doesn't hold water.
ex.ja: 君の説明はもっともらしいが、筋がちっとも通ってない。

ex.en: You're spitting out plausible lies.
ex.ja: もっともらしい嘘をつきやがって。

ex.en: A more plausible proposal is the one Leech presented in conjunction with Emmet's theory.
ex.ja: リーチがエメット理論との関連で提供した提案のほうがより妥当なものである。

note.ja: ラテン語 plaudere（拍手する）から。拍手に値しそうな →「もっともらしい・妥当な」。applause（拍手）と同じ。

en: A long or larger molecule consisting of a chain or network of many repeating units, formed by chemically bonding together many identical …
A material consisting of such polymer molecules.

polymer.ety: From poly- + -mer, from Ancient Greek πολύς (polús, “many”) + μέρος (méros, “part”). Coined by Jöns Jacob Berzelius in 1833, though his definition was quite different from the modern one.

note.ja: ギリシャ語 poly（多くの）+ meros（部分）。「多くの部分がつながったもの」→「重合体」。

en: Any or all of the forms of water particles, whether liquid or solid, that fall from the upper atmosphere (e.g., rain, hail, snow or sleet…
The amount of water precipitated in any form.

precipitation.ety: From Middle French précipitation, from Latin praecipitātiō, praecipitātiōnem. By surface analysis, precipitate + -ion.

note.ja: precipitate（落下させる）+ -ion。ラテン語 praeceps（真っ逆さまの）、prae + caput（頭）。「頭から落ちること」→「降水・沈殿」。

en: A period of 40 days, particularly
The 40-day period during which a widow is entitled to remain in her deceased husband's home while any dower is collected and returned.
To place into isolation to prevent the spread of any contagious disease.
To enter or stay in quarantine, particularly to self-quarantine to avoid an epidemic disease.

quarantine.ety:
From Medieval Latin quarentena and quarentīna (“40-day period, Lent”) via Middle English quarentine, Norman quarenteine, French quarenteine, and Italian quarantina, via proposed Late Latin *quaranta + -ēna (forming distributive adjectives), from Latin quadrāgintā (“four tens, 40”).
In reference to French politics, calque of French quarantaine after edicts of Louis IX. In reference to a severance of political relations, popularized by the Roosevelt administration's 1937 approach to the Axis powers and the later Kennedy administration's 1962 approach to Cuba during the missile crisis.

ex.en: People returning from Spain are required to self-quarantine for 14 days.
ex.ja: スペインから帰国する人全員に14日間の自主隔離を義務付けた。

ex.en: The hospital quarantined the infected patients to avoid cross infection.
ex.ja: 病院は院内感染を防ぐため、感染患者を隔離した。

note.ja: イタリア語 quaranta giorni（40日）から。ペスト流行時、船を40日間停泊させて隔離したことから。

en: A question, an inquiry (US), an enquiry (UK).
A question mark.
To ask a question.
To ask, inquire.

query.ety: An anglicisation of quere, an obsolete variant form of Latin quaere, second-person singular present active imperative of quaerō (“seek, look for; ask”); perhaps suffixed with -y (“abstract noun”). Cognate with French quérir, Italian chiedere, Portuguese querer, Romanian cere, and Spanish querer. Compare question.

ex.en: The saleswoman queried as she wrapped the gloves.
ex.ja: 美人店員は手袋を袋に包みながら尋ねた。

note.ja: ラテン語 quaere（尋ねよ）から。quer（求める・尋ねる）+ y。→「質問・問い合わせ・疑問」。
